newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha drops, June LSWR imports seen slow.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha drops, June LSWR imports seen slow.

text.p: Naphtha prices fell in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday in sympathy with a sharp loss in crude prices on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, market participants said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half July stood at $209.50/210.50 per tonne in late afternoon trade.
It changed hands at $212.00 in late Tuesday trading.
First-half July was assessed on par to slightly lower than the second half of the month.
On Tuesday, a South Korean trading firm sold a first-half July contract at $211.50.
In spreads, first-half July/first-half August was quoted at minus $1.50/minus 60 cents, compared with Tuesday's levels of minus 50 cents/even.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders shifted attention to possible sales to the United States as May requirements in Asia, including Japan, were mostly satisfied, traders said.
Japan's LSWR imports are expected to slow down in June as the price of domestically produced LSWR is gradually declining, they said.
